title: Grade 9 Science — Is Matter Pure? & Atoms and Molecules
description: Is Matter Around Us Pure? and Atoms and Molecules practice questions
subject: science

questions.question: A pure substance contains:
options: Only one type of particle (atoms or molecules)
questions.explanation: A pure substance has a fixed composition and contains only one type of particle (element: one type of atom; compound: one type of molecule). It cannot be separated by physical methods.

questions.question: An alloy like brass (copper and zinc) is a:
questions.explanation: Alloys are solutions of metals. Brass is a uniform (homogeneous) mixture of copper and zinc that cannot be separated by physical means. It has uniform composition throughout.

questions.question: The method used to separate a mixture of two miscible liquids with close boiling points is:
questions.explanation: Fractional distillation is used when two miscible liquids have boiling points close together (less than 25°C apart). Regular distillation cannot separate them efficiently.

questions.question: Colloids differ from true solutions in that:
options: Colloid particles are larger and can scatter light (Tyndall effect)
Colloid particles are smaller than in true solutions
questions.explanation: Colloid particles (1–1000 nm) are larger than solute particles in true solutions. They scatter light (Tyndall effect) and can be separated by centrifugation but not simple filtration.

questions.question: The Tyndall effect is the scattering of light by:
questions.explanation: The Tyndall effect occurs when colloidal particles scatter a beam of light, making the path of light visible. True solutions do not show this because their particles are too small.

questions.question: Water is a compound and not a mixture because:
options: It contains hydrogen and oxygen in any ratio
Hydrogen and oxygen are combined in a fixed ratio (2:1) and cannot be separated by physical means
It can be separated by evaporation
questions.explanation: In water (H₂O), hydrogen and oxygen are chemically combined in a fixed mass ratio of 1:8. The properties of water differ completely from its constituent elements.

questions.question: Which of the following is a heterogeneous mixture?
questions.explanation: Sand and water have non-uniform composition — sand particles are visibly separate from water. Salt solution, sugar solution, and air are homogeneous mixtures with uniform composition.

questions.question: Chromatography is used to separate:
options: Dissolved components in a mixture based on different rates of movement
questions.explanation: Chromatography separates components dissolved in a solvent (mobile phase) based on how they move through a stationary phase. Components with stronger affinity for the stationary phase move more slowly.

questions.question: Dalton's atomic theory states that atoms of the same element are:
options: Different in mass but same in shape
Identical in mass and chemical properties
questions.explanation: Dalton's atomic theory (1808): atoms of the same element are identical in mass and chemical properties. Atoms of different elements differ in mass and properties.

questions.question: The molecular formula of water tells us that one molecule of water contains:
questions.explanation: H₂O has 2 hydrogen atoms (subscript 2) and 1 oxygen atom. The subscript gives the number of atoms of each element in one molecule.

questions.question: The law of conservation of mass states that:
options: Mass can be created in chemical reactions
Total mass of reactants equals total mass of products in a chemical reaction
questions.explanation: Law of Conservation of Mass (Lavoisier): in a chemical reaction, the total mass of reactants equals the total mass of products. Mass is neither created nor destroyed.

questions.question: The molar mass of water (H₂O) is approximately:
questions.explanation: Molar mass of H₂O = 2(1) + 16 = 18 g/mol. Hydrogen has atomic mass 1 g/mol and oxygen has 16 g/mol.

questions.question: One mole of any substance contains:
questions.explanation: One mole = 6.022 × 10²³ particles (Avogadro's number). This applies to atoms, molecules, ions — any specified particle.

questions.question: The chemical formula of calcium carbonate is:
questions.explanation: Calcium (Ca²⁺) and carbonate (CO₃²⁻) combine in 1:1 ratio to form CaCO₃ — calcium carbonate (marble, limestone, chalk).

questions.question: The number of moles in 36 g of water (molar mass = 18 g/mol) is:
questions.explanation: Number of moles = mass / molar mass = 36 / 18 = 2 mol.
